evidence: find_signal_implementation_run (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-517) delegates to find_task_run and then checks only run.team_id == team_id, task.signal_report_id is not None, and not task.internal; it never compares the matched run's stored output.pr_url to the incoming PR on a branch match and carries no author identity. find_task_run's two legs key on caller-writable columns: output__pr_url (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:35-56) and TaskRun.branch (webhooks.py:64-79, filter(branch=branch, task__repository__iexact=repository, state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True).first()). Both columns are writable by any task:write caller: TaskRunViewSet.partial_update/set_output (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1075-1119, required_scopes task:write) feed update_task_run (facade/api.py:2040-2056: output merged via _apply_caller_output, then bare setattr for branch) and set_task_run_output (facade/api.py:2139-2160); TaskRunUpdateSerializer exposes branch and output (presentation/serializers.py:173-179); _apply_caller_output protects only pr_merged (_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS, facade/api.py:1770-1790). Control over the run is team-wide: _ensure_task_accessible(for_control=True) (views/api.py:852-866) -> task_accessible_for_run_view (facade/api.py:1807-1825) -> task_control_q (products/tasks/backend/visibility.py:22-45) grants every team member control of origin_product=signal_report tasks, and a member can also create such a task themselves (serializers.py:407-460 make origin_product, repository, signal_report, internal caller-settable; validate_signal_report only team-scopes at 616-619, validate_origin_product rejects only image_builder at 595-598). The webhook leg then treats the forged match as positive identification: _inbox_rereview_carve_out (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:144-231) requires only a head-changing action, _is_bot_authored (any Bot, tasks.py:124-127), head_repo == repo, an enabled config, the facade DTO, and an opted-in acting reviewer (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:144-156, resolved from the report's suggested reviewers, not from the PR); its provenance overrides the bot/draft/association pre-filter (tasks.py:876-881), the review-mode gate (tasks.py:944), and the author-write-permission gate (tasks.py:967-968), is stamped as output.inbox_review (tasks.py:1064), and becomes self_driving_review=True in the engine (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451; logic/reviewer.py:101-131). Concrete path: a team member with task:write and no GitHub write access PATCHes output.pr_url (or branch = the PR head ref) on any signal-report run in the team to point at a bot-authored, repo-native PR in the repo (their own PostHog Code task PR authored by the team App machine user via github_integration, or a dependabot PR); the next synchronize (an agent push they drive through the tasks product, or dependabot's rebase) enters the carve-out and stamphog reviews and can post a head-pinned APPROVE on a PR that was never a self-driving implementation, defeating the gates that tasks.py:100-103 says exist so an under-privileged author cannot obtain a branch-protection-satisfying approval. Tests never exercise a forged linkage: stamphog tests stub the facade (products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:32, 875-886) and the facade tests (products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1265-1320) create honest runs only.
notes: Distinct from the three neighbours. Cluster 2 (KA10 et al.) is the receiver leg having no linkage at all and explicitly holds up the webhook leg as the safe model; LA15 shows the webhook leg's linkage is forgeable through the same caller-writable run fields, so KA10's second suggested remedy (make the receiver leg require bot authorship + repo-native head + a facade match) would leave both legs open. Cluster 73 (S10, consider) is accidental stale-run mis-binding via the branch fallback with no adversary. Cluster 75 (E1) is the any-bot floor with another installed bot as the attacker; requiring the expected App bot login does not close LA15 because App-authored non-inbox Code PRs still qualify. Adding pr_url to _WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS (KA10's first remedy) is also insufficient on its own because TaskRun.branch stays PATCHable and the branch leg still binds. Verdict would drop to not_real if the tasks API rejected caller writes to both output.pr_url and branch on signal-report runs (or the facade required a server-recorded linkage such as the webhook backstop's _record_run_pr_url, webhooks.py:157-166, which does verify a repo-native head), or if task_control_q stopped granting every team member control of signal_report tasks; it would drop to should_fix if the carve-out additionally verified the PR author is the team's own App machine user AND the run's task was auto-started by Signals rather than API-created.
